- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.2) mid-horizon, adjust forecast downward by 3–8% to reflect risk aversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price drops after peaks), apply a 2–5% downward bias to avoid overreacting to recent spikes.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more) and forecast is erratic, smooth out extremes by averaging adjacent forecast points.  
- When true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially in 30d horizon), apply a 3–7% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If forecast spikes >10% above recent 10-day average and sentiment is weak or negative, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overconfidence.  
- For 30d forecasts with high sentiment volatility, use a 3-day moving average of true outcomes to anchor correction.
